note: GetPropertyIdentifierLocation resolves the location from property.ContainingType instead of the property, so the cast never matches and the diagnostic location becomes null (then silently dropped by the filter).

hits.issue: Using `property.ContainingType.DeclaringSyntaxReferences` retrieves the syntax of the containing type (e.g., class or struct) rather than the property itself. This will never cast to `PropertyDeclarationSyntax`, causing the method to always return null and silently swallow the diagnostic for all source-declared properties.

GetPropertyIdentifierLocation reads `property.ContainingType.DeclaringSyntaxReferences` instead of `property.DeclaringSyntaxReferences`. The syntax it gets is a type declaration, so the `as PropertyDeclarationSyntax` cast always yields null. The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic (used at line 985) therefore always has no location and is now silently dropped by the filter, including for source-declared properties. This is a regression of an existing diagnostic and contradicts C4, C5 and C10.
